mathgap.title: Direct count assignment
mathgap.principle: When a statement explicitly gives a numeric count for a person, set that person's current count to the given value immediately.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any statement of the form "X has N items" (e.g., "Meyer has 41 potatoes").
mathgap.example: Leaving a person's count undefined after reading "X has N potatoes" instead of setting it to N.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer
mathgap.principle: Interpret "X has N more than Y" as X = Y + N, and "X has N fewer than Y" as X = Y - N, preserving the order of the named persons.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Statements that compare two persons using "more" or "fewer" (e.g., "Arlie has 13 more potatoes than Malcolm").
mathgap.example: Interpreting "X has N more potatoes than Y" as X = N, ignoring Y's count.

mathgap.title: Zero‑difference relational handling
mathgap.principle: When a relational statement involves a zero difference (e.g., "X has 0 more potatoes than Y"), treat it as an equality X = Y, not as a direct count of zero.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any statement of the form "X has 0 more ... than Y" or a signed‑difference equality where the numeric difference is zero.
mathgap.example: Treating "Mckenzie has 0 more potatoes than Harve" as setting Mckenzie to 0 instead of equating Mckenzie with Harve.

mathgap.title: Sequential transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For a transfer "X gives N items to Y", subtract N from X's current count and add N to Y's current count, updating the state immediately.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Statements describing a one‑way transfer of items (e.g., "Ignacio gives 1 potato to Mallory").
mathgap.example: For "X gives N potatoes to Y", adding N to X and subtracting N from Y (reversing the direction).

mathgap.title: Signed‑difference substitution
mathgap.principle: If a signed difference (X − Y) appears in an equation and its numeric value is already known, replace the whole expression with that numeric value in all other equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a previously solved signed difference is used in a later equation.
mathgap.example: Failing to replace a known signed difference (A − B = 5) with 5 in subsequent equations, leaving it symbolic.

mathgap.title: Chronological evaluation
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the exact order they appear; later statements must use the counts after all earlier updates (transfers, assignments, etc.) have been applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any multi‑statement problem where earlier actions can affect later references.
mathgap.example: Evaluating a later statement using counts before earlier transfers have been applied.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For a transfer that is conditional on a count, first evaluate the condition using the current counts; only if the condition holds should the transfer be applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Statements of the form "If X has more than N items, X gives ..." (e.g., the Marcel conditional in the Katrina problem).
mathgap.example: Applying a conditional transfer without checking the condition, e.g., transferring Marcel's oranges even when he has ≤7.

mathgap.title: Target variable dependency analysis
mathgap.principle: Identify which equations and variables directly or indirectly affect the queried person, and ignore all unrelated statements when solving for the target.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem contains many statements, most of which are irrelevant to the final query.
mathgap.example: Including unrelated equations in the solution process, causing unnecessary complexity and potential errors.

mathgap.title: Signed difference equality parsing
mathgap.principle: Parse statements of the form "The number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of potatoes that C and D have" as the signed equation (A − B) = (C − D), preserving the order of names on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence uses the phrasing "has more than" together with "difference between" two other persons.
mathgap.example: Parsing the equality as (A − B) = (D − C) or as an absolute difference, swapping the order of C and D.

mathgap.title: Solve signed difference equations with unknowns
mathgap.principle: When a signed‑difference equality (A − B) = (C − D) contains unknown variables, rearrange it into a linear equation and solve for one variable in terms of the others, propagating the relation through the system.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any signed‑difference equality where not all four variables are already known.
mathgap.example: Leaving the equation (A − B) = (C − D) unsolved instead of rearranging to express, for example, A = B + C − D.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences or swapping term order
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses the signed nature of the difference with an absolute value, or misorders the terms on the right‑hand side.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Parse signed difference equalities exactly as (A − B) = (C − D), preserving the order of names on each side.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats transfers as independent of order, applying them simultaneously or out of sequence.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process statements strictly in the order given, updating counts after each transfer before evaluating later statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats direct count assignments as immutable, not accounting for later transfers that modify them.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat explicit counts as initial values that can be changed by subsequent transfers; update the count accordingly.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model skips conditional transfers entirely, treating them as if they never occur.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Evaluate the condition using current counts; if true, apply the transfer, otherwise do nothing.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting multiplicative increase statements as additive
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model adds the increase amount instead of multiplying, treating "increase by 4/3 times" as "+4/3".
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret multiplicative increase as a scaling factor: new = old × factor.
